title: Why Ice Ages Run on a 100,000-Year Clock
core_question: What sets the planet's ice-age rhythm, and why does the 100,000-year beat still not fully match the theory?
why_they_click: Tiny wobbles in Earth's orbit pace the ice, but the biggest cycle is the one the maths explains worst.
data_source: NOAA NCEI Paleoclimatology; NASA orbital-cycle explainers; peer-reviewed ice-core and Milankovitch studies
evidence: "ice age explained" is up 1680% over five years, the strongest rising signal available.
